title: Accurate Leakage Speculation for Quantum Error Correction
problem: Physical qubits in quantum error correction (QEC) can leak into higher energy states (e.g., |2>), corrupting syndrome measurements and spreading errors to neighboring qubits; detecting leakage on data qubits is especially hard because they are never directly measured during QEC cycles.
motivation: As QEC codes scale to larger distances, even rare leakage events accumulate and paralyze syndrome extraction, and existing heuristic leakage detectors (e.g., eraser) have high false-positive rates that trigger unnecessary Leakage Reduction Circuits (LRCs), introducing additional gate errors and extending QEC cycle latency.
method: GLADIATOR detects qubit leakage (when qubits jump to unwanted higher energy states) using a probabilistic graph where nodes are syndrome patterns (error-checking readouts) and edges show how likely each pattern is under leakage versus regular errors, calibrated to the actual device. Offline, it labels patterns dominated by leakage-induced transitions and stores them in a lookup table. Online, each quantum error-correction cycle observes a 5-bit syndrome per qubit and uses a tiny classifier (at most 10 LUTs per qubit—the basic logic building blocks on a chip) to recognize it in under 1 nanosecond, triggering recovery only for flagged patterns; GLADIATOR-D extends this with two cycles of syndrome history and works across surface, color, and qLDPC codes.
key_novelty: GLADIATOR uses a probabilistic graph-labeling framework with calibrated transition probabilities to distinguish leakage-induced syndrome patterns from regular-error patterns while reducing hardware overhead to 10 LUTs per qubit—versus 177–5393 for prior work—across different quantum error-correction codes.
contributions: GLADIATOR: a code-aware offline error-propagation graph construction and online syndrome lookup table for accurate leakage speculation across surface, color, and qLDPC codes
Reduction of unnecessary LRCs by up to 3x (2x average) vs. eraser, and 1.73x less leakage population growth
Hardware implementation requiring <0.1% LUTs at code distance 25 (17x-63x reduction vs. eraser on Kintex UltraScale+ FPGA)
Analysis of structured open-loop staggered LRC scheduling as a competitive baseline to motivate closed-loop approaches

metrics.speedup: 1.7x-3.9x QEC cycle speedup vs. always-LRC baseline
metrics.area: <0.1% LUTs at code distance 25 on Kintex UltraScale+ FPGA; 10 LUTs per data qubit
metrics.accuracy: 16% reduction in logical error rate; 1.91x lower false-positive rate vs. eraser
metrics.other: 17x-63x FPGA LUT reduction vs. eraser across code distances 5-25; combinational logic evaluates in <1 ns

limitations: GLADIATOR's graphical model must be rebuilt for each QEC code and re-calibrated when device noise drifts significantly; the two-round windowed variant (GLADIATOR-D) adds latency that may constrain real-time QEC controller timing.
primary_theme: accurate leakage speculation for quantum error correction
